The UN-FITTED twin of our 0.958 artifact, submitted as a private-split hedge rather than for public score. This kernel therefore holds a public-tuned and an un-tuned twin with identical recipe otherwise, so the deadline choice is between two real artifacts instead of one. Audited per cell: exactly one cell changed, and only by the line-anchored W_RAPTOR_C substitution. Run verified: blend_receipt carries lateral_oa 0.5 (flat), a224 0.35, and S6 stage PASS with '[s6] folded into the compact half at 0.4 over 3 studies'.

Discriminates a disagreement between our measurement and an independent team's. Themselves (goodpjw2008/rsna-knee-does-s6-help-next-to-r6) report that adding nartaa's S6 all-data model next to R6 costs 0.001 -- 0.957 against 0.958 for the same recipe without it -- and conclude 'do not add S6 to R6'. Our own three shots of the same arm displayed 0.958 at shares 0.40, 0.40-with-flat-weights and 0.60, i.e. no visible cost. Both observations sit inside the public half's noise, so the way to separate them is to push the share where S6 dominates: here compact = 0.20*rank(R6) + 0.80*rank(S6). If this drops to 0.957 their result is weight-dependent and the two measurements reconcile; if it also displays 0.958 then the share is harmless all the way to 0.80 and their result is more likely an implementation difference than the model. Base = the same construction as 57250245 (byte-for-byte fork of heliosli/blend-mine-in-private-lb-luck-to-all-upvoters, R6 frozen bundle, Raptor-384 with anatomical mirror + 224-crop at A224=0.35, per-finding weights as the author set them). Run verified: S6 stage PASS, arm E_prior, 3/3 scored, 0 fallbacks, log '[s6] folded into the compact half at 0.8 over 3 studies'. Fail-safe: any S6 failure leaves the base submission byte-identical.

Adds the anatomical-mirror view to the 224-crop Raptor arm -- a component the published 0.956 lineage has and our base was missing. Verified by counting the code: in our base the 384 arm already averages plain and mirrored views (gpu_windows(..., mirror=True) plus infer_pair_probs), but _mirror_tri, mirror=True and infer_pair_probs appear ZERO times in the 224 arm's script. The published fix describes the result exactly: nartaa's 224 checkpoint 'was published with one view only', and giving it the mirror left the displayed score unchanged at 0.956 while moving rank 357 -> 289, from bronze back into silver. That is a within-band gain, which is precisely what matters here: our 0.958 band holds ~1155 teams and the silver cut is about 70 places ahead of us, so a rank improvement inside the band is real. Ported by taking that notebook's 224 script verbatim (nartaa's own _mirror_tri, SLOT_SIZES, _slot_index, the mirror= parameter and the 0.5*(plain+mirrored) average) and putting our three raptor224_raw.csv lines back, because the blend cell reads that file; audited so that exactly one cell changed and removing those three lines restores their script byte-for-byte. The written 224 script compiles on its own. Base otherwise identical to 57250245 (byte-for-byte fork of heliosli/blend-mine-in-private-lb-luck-to-all-upvoters, R6 frozen bundle, 384 arm with mirror, A224=0.35, author's per-finding weights, no S6). Run verified: RAPTOR224_STAGE completed with raptor224_failed 0 in 24.8 s, both raptor224_raw.csv and raptor224_sub.csv written, blend receipt a224=0.35. Splits the 224-crop arm's share between its plain and its mirror-averaged view -- a component the published 0.957 recipe uses and our base was discarding. Verbatim from laimerbotrolenk/rsna-four-model-ensemble: 'TTA is the arithmetic mean of the plain and mirrored probabilities, then ranked per finding. Mixing these ranks is not equivalent to changing the probability average to 75/25', with weights Raptor-384 TTA 32.5% + Raptor-224 plain 8.75% + Raptor-224 TTA 8.75% -- i.e. 384 keeps 0.65 and the 224 share 0.35 is split in half. Crucially 'the plain 224 forward already runs in the supplied code', so this costs no extra forward passes: our mirrored 224 stage was computing infer_probs(model, xw) and throwing it away inside the 0.5*(plain+mirror) average. Four asserted patches: keep arm_plain, store the plain result, dump raptor224_plain.csv, and in the blend average the 224 TTA rank with the 224 plain rank BEFORE the author's (1-A224)*r384 + A224*r224 is applied -- so the author's expression itself is untouched and this is exactly 'split the 224 share'. Base otherwise identical to 57250245 (byte-for-byte fork of heliosli/blend-mine-in-private-lb-luck-to-all-upvoters, R6 frozen bundle, 384 arm with mirror, 224 arm with mirror, author's per-finding weights, no S6). Run verified: raptor224_plain.csv written (704 bytes), raptor224_raw.csv and raptor224_sub.csv also present, log line '[s9b] 224 plain view loaded'. Fail-safe: if the plain file is missing, malformed or has the wrong rows the blend is byte-identical to the m224 twin.

Splits the 384-crop arm's share between its plain and its mirror-averaged view, matching what its sibling 57377106 already does for the 224 arm. The 384 arm's infer_pair_probs computed the plain probabilities and returned only 0.5*(plain+mirror), so the plain half was being discarded -- the same waste the 224 arm had. Mixing those two ranks is not the same as averaging their probabilities, so the 384 share (0.65 of the Raptor half, four times the 224 arm's) is now half plain and half TTA. No extra forward passes: the plain probabilities were already computed. Build: infer_pair_probs returns the plain half too, the single call site stores both, the stage dumps raptor_plain.csv, and the blend averages the 384 TTA rank with the 384 plain rank BEFORE the author's (1-A224)*r384 + A224*r224 is applied, i.e. the author's expression itself is untouched. Base = the m224p kernel, so this also carries the 224 mirror and the 224 plain/TTA split, R6 compact half, author's per-finding weights, no S6. Run verified: logs '[s9c] 384 plain view loaded' and '[s9b] 224 plain view loaded', and all six prediction CSVs are present (raptor_plain.csv 709 B, raptor_raw.csv, raptor_sub.csv, raptor224_plain.csv 699 B, raptor224_raw.csv, raptor224_sub.csv). HONEST NOTE: unlike the 224 mirror, this split has no measured backing anywhere -- the published table keeps the 384 arm as a single TTA slot and calls its own weights 'an unvalidated hypothesis'. Splitting the 384 arm is one step past even that, so this is a test, not a known gain. Fail-safe: a missing or malformed plain file leaves the blend byte-identical to its parent.
